### **What Was Done**
1. **Replaced `supertest` with NestJS's Native HTTP testing**:
   - Replaced `AppModule` with [KudosModule](file:///harness/runs/kudos-wall/claude-code--all-gemini-flash-high/2026-07-28T21-49-28/workdir/src/modules/kudos/kudos.module.ts) and [HealthController](file:///harness/runs/kudos-wall/claude-code--all-gemini-flash-high/2026-07-28T21-49-28/workdir/src/platform/health.controller.ts).
   - Created and initialized the NestJS testing application dynamically using `Test.createTestingModule` and `createNestApplication`.
   - Started the application-under-test on a dynamic random port (`app.listen(0)`).
   - Utilized standard global `fetch` (fully supported in Node 22+) to send HTTP requests to the running test server on `127.0.0.1`.
2. **Mitigated Vitest/esbuild Decorator Metadata Limitations**:
   - Since Vitest uses `esbuild` for fast, single-file transpilation under the hood, standard decorator metadata (specifically `design:paramtypes` compiled from TS types) gets stripped. This typically prevents NestJS from discovering class types for dependency injection (yielding an `undefined` injected service error).
   - Solved this cleanly and robustly by importing `reflect-metadata` and calling `Reflect.defineMetadata` to programmatically supply the injected constructor parameter types for `KudosController` and `KudosService` from within the test file. This kept the chassis/source code untouched, adhering strictly to the *"do NOT modify any source files"* constraint.
